description:
Read only the profiler report from the previous task and produce an executable NAS search space plan in JSON.
Behavior requirements: - Be conservative and pragmatic. - Prefer simple, well-established model families. - Include only model families clearly supported by profiler evidence. - Use small, bounded, realistic hyperparameter ranges. - Prefer categorical choices and small discrete ranges over wide continuous spaces. - Express uncertainty when profiler evidence is incomplete.
Strict constraints: - Do not inspect raw datasets. - Do not call dataset inspection tools. - Do not train models. - Do not run Optuna. - Do not evaluate model performance. - Do not select a final model.
Output must be strict JSON only (no markdown, no code fences, no prose before/after JSON).
\n\nInput: use only the profiler report generated by the previous task.

selected_model_families.rationale: Profiler identifies the data as a 1D signal (ECG). 1D-CNNs are the standard approach for extracting local features from signals while sharing weights to reduce parameter count compared to dense layers.
Included as a baseline model; however, requires significant bottlenecking and regularization to handle the 2500:160 feature-to-sample ratio.

uncertainty_notes: Temporal resolution (sampling frequency) is unknown, making it difficult to optimize kernel sizes for specific physical ECG components (e.g., QRS complex).
The 160 samples may not be representative of the broader 'Sleep Apnea' population variance.
Signal-to-noise ratio is unknown, which may impact the effectiveness of deeper architectures.
handoff_notes: Critical: Input must be reshaped from (160, 2500) to (160, 2500, 1) for cnn1d.
Due to the small dataset size (n=160), the optimization stage must use stratified K-fold cross-validation (k=5 or 10) to prevent misleading performance metrics.
Strong weight decay (L2 regularization) should be applied globally across all candidate models.
Global Average Pooling is recommended before the final dense layer in CNNs to minimize the parameter count.
